text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The National Assembly is expected to pass seven bills at its next session, which begins on April 2.
-- The Asian Development Bank has proposed a $1.5 billion loan programme for Vietnam between 1997-2000.
-- Vietnam has asked the European Union to increase its import quota for locally-made garments and textiles.
-- The seventh Francophonie Summit will take place in Hanoi between November 14 and 16 this year.

-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam has told visiting Thai Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn that Thailand should respect Vietnamese sea territory to avoid incidents which might harm bilateral relations.
-- More than 1,880 smuggling and trade fraud cases were discovered in the first two months of 1997.
-- Vietnam has pledged its committment to the creation of favourable conditions for the construction of a road linking Vietnam, Laos and Thailand.
-- An eight-day appeal trial will be held in late March for fifteen defendents involved in the Tamexco corruption case.
